title: X OAuth 2.0 client ids, user ids, placeholders and masked displays
summary: A public client id in an authorization request, a user id in a response, Bearer and Basic placeholders, environment and template references, masked displays and a scheme with no value.
rationale: A client id and a user id are public identifiers and not tokens or secrets. A placeholder, reference or masked display carries no value, and a scheme with no value holds nothing to flag. Flagging them would redact identifiers and documentation a reader needs. The case makes no statement about percent-containing shapes.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: these inputs hold no token or secret value. That a client id and a user id are public and that a placeholder, reference or masked display is not a value are the project's decisions; X documents the carriers, not the confidentiality of an id.
